memoryTip: Mallet-able metal — can be shaped; open to influence.
correctPassage: Public opinion on the issue remains malleable, especially among younger voters.
wrongPassages: She packed a malleable suitcase: one shirt and a book for a month abroad.
The mall’s malleable daylight film turned every storefront the same amber.
Boards tabled the malleable proposal community letters had supported.

definition: well chosen or suited to the circumstances
memoryTip: Felicity = happiness/aptness — a happily well-chosen word.
correctPassage: It was a felicitous choice of words that captured the mood exactly.
wrongPassages: The ice ramp felt felicitous after crews salted it like a city sidewalk.
Committees shelved the felicitous pilot users had rated highest overall.
The slip’s felicitous freeboard marks were worn down to bare metal.

definition: extreme care and attention to detail
memoryTip: Meticulous = tiny details — extreme care.
correctPassage: The restorer’s meticulousness is visible in every repaired seam.
wrongPassages: The glossary defined meticulousness as “see page 2” and never returned to it.
The mug-measure of meticulousness varied with every baker in the test kitchen.
The drawer of meticulousness held one key that opened nothing in the building.

memoryTip: In-vigor: put vigor in — energize.
correctPassage: A change of leadership can invigorate an organization that has grown stagnant.
wrongPassages: He moved to invigorate the warrant by wiping the phone before surrendering it.
The cron will invigorate the backlog metrics by resetting counters at midnight.
She hoped to invigorate the mutiny by banning the word “union” in email.

memoryTip: Priest-clean pure — unspoiled original condition.
correctPassage: Hikers are asked to leave the trail as pristine as they found it.
wrongPassages: Committees cut the pristine translation budget that clinics still needed.
Committees shelved the pristine pilot that had the highest user rating.
a pristine tabletop report is a photo of the whiteboard after it was wiped.

memoryTip: De-rogate: take away from dignity — detract.
correctPassage: Nothing in the agreement should derogate from existing labor rights.
wrongPassages: He tried to derogate the gag by discussing details as “publicly known.”
They aimed to derogate vacancy by building more towers that stayed empty.
They tried to derogate the mold by turning up the heat without fixing the leak.

memoryTip: Venus-level respect — treat as sacred / deeply respect.
correctPassage: Many still venerate the founders while questioning later policy choices.
wrongPassages: They tried to venerate the landslide by paving without checking the drainage.
The agent will venerate the survey by auto-filling five stars for every chat.
She hoped the gift would venerate the insult; it only reminded everyone of it.

memoryTip: Light heart — cheerful, not heavy or serious.
correctPassage: A light-hearted tone made the difficult subject easier to discuss.
wrongPassages: The funeral oration was light-hearted only if solemn and slow counts as light.
Her light-hearted lawsuit demanded years of damages for a broken mug.
The light-hearted safety chapter listed only the most severe injury protocols.

memoryTip: Like precipitation falling suddenly — cause to happen fast (or rash).
correctPassage: A sudden price spike can precipitate panic selling.
wrongPassages: The team will precipitate the outage by rebooting the same failing node repeatedly.
The software will precipitate drafts by saving them under random filenames.
He moved to precipitate the subpoena by claiming the account was never his.

memoryTip: Scrutiny = close look — examine carefully.
correctPassage: Peer reviewers will scrutinize every claim before the paper is accepted.
wrongPassages: Editors scrutinize submissions by reading only the title and never opening the file.
She scrutinized the horizon for half a second and declared nothing of interest.
To scrutinize the budget, the board shredded it unread and approved a replacement on instinct.

memoryTip: Ambi = both — mixed feelings both ways.
correctPassage: She felt ambivalent about leaving a job she both loved and resented.
wrongPassages: He was ambivalent: completely for the plan and free of any reservation.
Her ambivalent vote was a clear yes on every line of the proposal.
Ambivalent supporters filled the hall with one unbroken chant of approval.

memoryTip: By analogy — comparing similar structures.
correctPassage: The argument is analogical: it treats cities as if they were living organisms.
wrongPassages: Funds chased analogical yield in a product that never paid a coupon.
The rupture disc was analogical: rated above the header’s design pressure.
The subtonic held was analogical under a final major triad on I.

definition: cause two or more to change places
memoryTip: Trans-pose: switch places or keys.
correctPassage: Students were asked to transpose the melody into a different key.
wrongPassages: The bot will transpose ticket age by bulk-closing anything older than seven days.
They hoped to transpose the recall by changing the product’s name only.
They hoped to transpose the protest optics by filming empty chairs as consensus.

definition: the quality of being open and honest
memoryTip: Candid camera honesty — open frankness.
correctPassage: His candor about past mistakes earned him unexpected support.
wrongPassages: She kept a candor spare in the glove box next to registration papers.
The cask branded candor held spare hose washers and a gauge.
The lobby playlist’s candor was one looped track at constant volume.

memoryTip: Prudent choices — careful good sense.
correctPassage: Fiscal prudence kept the university solvent during the downturn.
wrongPassages: He tossed a foam block labeled prudence into the trunk “just in case.”
He treated prudence as an unit of flour in a parody cookbook.
The utility bin prudence mixed batteries with binder clips.

memoryTip: Equity = fairness — impartial and just.
correctPassage: An equitable distribution of resources was the panel’s main goal.
wrongPassages: The safety valve was equitable and never lifted during the pressure test.
The speech was equitable in the sense that it never risked a single contested claim.
The wharf’s equitable crane load chart was for equipment long since scrapped.

definition: not able to be reached or achieved
memoryTip: Can’t attain it — out of reach.
correctPassage: Perfection is unattainable, but steady improvement is not.
wrongPassages: The ascent felt unattainable inside a pressurized cabin to the summit hotel.
Her unattainable interrogatory set asked for every email ever sent by anyone.
The savanna looked unattainable after fire and rain restarted the grass cycle.

memoryTip: Vapor-thin flavor — bland, empty of interest.
correctPassage: The speech was elegant in form but vapid in content.
wrongPassages: The serac zone felt vapid from a marked snow bridge with fixed ropes.
a vapid load test hits one request and graphs a single point.
a vapid majority of one vote was recorded in the minutes as unanimous consent.

definition: a penalty for disobeying; or official permission
memoryTip: Two-faced: punish (sanctions) or officially allow — context decides.
correctPassage: The league may sanction the team for violating recruitment rules.
wrongPassages: Obsolete packing art including the sanction wrench doodle was purged.
Deleting thumbs.db finally made folder sanction truly empty.
He packed emergency sanction next to flares that had expired years ago.

definition: the state of being out of place
memoryTip: Incongruous mismatch — things that don’t fit together.
correctPassage: There is a striking incongruity between the firm’s green claims and its emissions.
wrongPassages: The museum stored its incongruity in a drawer marked miscellaneous hardware.
She earned a weekend certificate in practical incongruity using consumer spreadsheets.
She enabled incongruity mode that only dimmed the wallpaper.
